hardware_chipset.chipset: Intel H81 Express / 8 Series-C220, identified locally by board DMI and PCI IDs

platform_conclusion.reason: The CPU supports VT-d, but the identified Intel H81 chipset specification says VT-d=No. A BIOS toggle or kernel parameter cannot be treated as a valid solution for this identified chipset.
platform_conclusion.caveat: Intel's page warns that feature availability depends on the complete system; no contrary board implementation was found locally, so this is the strongest supported platform conclusion.

group_target.reason: No IOMMU group is exposed while the platform IOMMU is not active.

C_IOMMU_GROUP_SAFETY.interpretation: The Linux VFIO model makes an IOMMU group the unit of ownership; without groups, no SAFE_CANDIDATE classification is defensible.

F_HOST_GRAPHICS.guest_gpu: RX550 1002:699f at 0000:01:00.0 is only a candidate; it is not assigned
F_HOST_GRAPHICS.reason: Current KWin supportInformation and glxinfo directly report RX550 as the OpenGL renderer. Physical monitor attachment to Intel does not establish renderer independence.

G_RESET_REATTACH.reset_capability_detail: NOT_AVAILABLE: unprivileged lspci capability access was denied; sudo read-only access required a password; no reset was attempted.
G_RESET_REATTACH.amdgpu_recovery_evidence: Kernel log reports Polaris12 initialization and Using BACO for runtime pm; no successful guest detach/reattach test exists.
G_RESET_REATTACH.interpretation: A reset method/interface existing is not proof that FLR, bus reset, or reattachment will succeed for this RX550 after QEMU/libvirt releases it.

H_HDMI_AUDIO.kernel_binding: snd_hda_intel bound to 0000:01:00.0 through amdgpu audio component
H_HDMI_AUDIO.guest_audio_assignment: SUPPORTED_CONDITIONAL: if the guest needs HDMI/DP audio, 01:00.1 must be considered with 01:00.0; the actual IOMMU group and guest driver behavior are not validated.
H_HDMI_AUDIO.risk: Leaving 01:00.1 on the host while assigning only 01:00.0 may leave an audio function/driver conflict; assigning it without a validated group may make the group non-viable.

I_EXISTING_VM.reason: libvirt/virsh/QEMU management tools and configuration directories are absent in the current runtime; no VM was created or modified.
I_EXISTING_VM.do_not_infer: Do not convert NOT_AVAILABLE into NO_EXISTING_VM.

J_STORAGE.reason: The SATA controller is identified, but no IOMMU groups exist to prove whether it shares a group with the RX550. It must not be assigned or touched.

K_REVERSIBILITY.detail: No system change; no rollback required.
H81 is identified and Intel documents VT-d=No; changing motherboard/chipset is outside current scope and higher risk than a BIOS toggle.

K_REVERSIBILITY.step: Enable VT-d in BIOS/kernel on compatible hardware
K_REVERSIBILITY.detail: Would require firmware and boot-time changes plus reboot; not a valid remedy for the identified H81 specification.
Conceptually reversible by removing boot configuration and rebuilding/restoring initramfs; not performed.

K_REVERSIBILITY.step: Bind RX550 display/audio functions to vfio-pci
K_REVERSIBILITY.detail: Requires validated IOMMU group, all group functions handled, client shutdown, and reset/reattach proof; current host renderer depends on RX550.
Domain definition can be removed, but physical device reattachment and host recovery are not validated.
Requires successful reset, no active host clients, and driver rebind; none was tested.
Could be conceptually reversible, but current KWin/Xwayland renderer evidence shows RX550 is active; not tested.

L_RISKS.detail: KWin reports RX550 as OpenGL renderer; monitor output being on Intel does not prevent loss of compositor/Xwayland rendering.
H81 official VT-d=No and current groups=0.
01:00.1 is a bound HDMI audio function associated with 01:00.0.
amdgpu currently owns 01:00.0; vfio-pci is not bound; libvirt would need a valid detach/attach lifecycle.
Only a reset interface was observed; no guest detach/reattach test exists.
Intel connector is active, but current compositor renderer is RX550.
/dev/sda is behind 00:1f.2; group sharing cannot be tested while IOMMU is unavailable.
Persistent VFIO/IOMMU/driver binding normally requires reboot; no reboot was performed.
Project recovery gate remains FAIL and no VFIO-specific independent recovery was validated.
sudo read-only inspection was unavailable due password requirement; no root namespace or full FD inventory is claimed.
